question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund is being set up in GIFT-IFSC as a Category III AIF, registering as an FPI under SEBI (FPI) Regulations 2019. What is the mandatory sponsor commitment in the fund for this Cat III AIF-FPI?

answer.text: 2.5% of corpus or USD 750,000, whichever is lower
5% of corpus or USD 1.5 million, whichever is lower
10% of corpus or USD 5 million, whichever is lower
No sponsor commitment required for IFSC-domiciled AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI (FPI) Regulations 2019 read with RBI May 12, 2021 circular, an IFSC-domiciled Cat III AIF registering as FPI must have Sponsor Commitment of 5% of corpus OR USD 1.5 million, whichever is LOWER. Cat I/II in IFSC has 2.5% OR USD 750,000 whichever lower. The Trap: Option A is Cat I/II figure. Option C is invented. Option D is wrong — sponsor commitment mandatory. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B, XIX-C test IFSC sponsor commits. XIX-E tests Cat III specific figures. Manager's Pro-Tip: The USD cap often binds before the 5% of corpus for large IFSC funds. Design the sponsor vehicle in a jurisdiction that permits USD capitalisation with minimum FATCA leakage.
